callee.behavior: [rdi + 0x10] + 0x3e (62), returned in rax; this entry discards that return

callee_census.other_sites_note: census only; the other nine sites' enclosing functions are not modelled here, and this packet claims the field-sum loop, not exclusive ownership of the shared callee

caller_census.method: full .text disassembly scan for e8 rel32 calls and e9 rel32 jumps to 0x514bcd0

container_chain.entry_first_qword: address of a slot; the slot's content is the callee argument (the loop loads [cursor], then [that value], before the call); the same slot value is reloaded after the call to read the +0x50 field

notes: Instruction-level detail lives only in the raw objdump excerpts; this JSON holds semantic records only.
The endbr64 at 0x514bcd0 and the endbr64 at 0x5032f40 are genuine instructions in the target binary, not placeholders; the nopl at 0x514bd01 is genuine alignment padding before the loop head.
The callee has no int3 padding: its FDE ends at 0x5032f4d and the following bytes belong to another function's tail, so padding_bytes is 0, not a missing record.
The entry's own FDE range ends at 0x514bd38; the 8 int3 bytes to the next FDE at 0x514bd40 are padding, verified byte-for-byte.

The callee return is overwritten without use: after the call, the loop reloads the entry's first qword and adds the qword at +0x50 of that slot value. Whether the call is load-bearing (a side effect) or dead is not claimed; the model calls the callee once per entry and discards its return, exactly as the bytes do.

This entry is the following FDE after the range-sum function 0x514bc60 (open PR #1346 in the same series) and shares its container chain and callee, but its accumulation rule is different: #1346 sums the callee return, this entry sums the +0x50 field and discards the callee return. The two are not the same claim.
The container chain ([rdi+0x788], then +0x30, then the +0xb18/+0xb20 range) is transliterated, not typed: no source-level type name is claimed for any link.
objdump's nearest-symbol annotations are explicitly not claimed as symbol names.

rule.accumulation: plain 64-bit wrapping add (add 0x50(%rax),%rbp); no saturation, no overflow check
rule.arguments: rdi = input object, rsi = out pointer
rule.callee_call_per_entry: exactly one call to 0x5032f40 per entry, with rdi = the qword stored at the address held in entry + 0x0; the returned rax is overwritten by the reload at 0x514bd17 and never contributes to the sum
rule.empty_range: begin == end skips the loop via the je at 0x514bcff; [rsi] = 0, return 1
rule.per_entry: contribution = the qword at [slot + 0x50], where slot = the qword stored in entry + 0x0 (the loop loads [cursor] into rax, advances the cursor by 0x10, loads [rax] into rdi, calls the callee, then reloads [cursor - 0x10] into rax and adds 0x50(%rax))
rule.result: return 1 always; [rsi] = sum over the range, 0 for an empty range
